question: What is the meaning of spare parts information in relation to service information?
description: The spare parts information in relation to service information refers to the availability and source of spare parts for the repair of a product. This information is provided as supplementary information to the statement about the ability to repair the product (5.2.1.08). If the statement is set to false, it means that there are no spare parts available for the product. The results of a reliability assessment support identifying appropriate spare parts. This information is relevant to a broad range of products and depends on the type of product, components, and technologies used in manufacturing, as well as the nature of failures typically encountered with the product during its lifetime. The identification of priority parts can also be used for PCDS statements related to upgradability. The support-related aspects, such as the availability of diagnosis support, spare parts, repair information, and repair services, particularly when repairs are complex or require a specific technical skill set, should also be considered. This is further described in EN 45554:2020, Clause 7 (for energy-related products).

Guide to Passports for the Construction Sector 
57 
 
 
Figure B.2 – Timeline of the useful life of a structure 
If we zoom in on the information that the stakeholder needs to 
provide for a passport, we get the following list: 
Client 
● Management of the assets: materials and the corresponding raw 
materials, types of connections, specific service lives and 
possibly measurement data. 
● Value of assets quantified: materials, raw materials, types of 
connections, surface area and quantities, technical condition of 
construction elements, residual service life, financial value. 
● Tracing the owner of leased products. 
● Service life extension of assets (possibly with other function): 
technical condition of construction elements, construction 
elements’ load, residual service life, design principles, building 
physics aspects. 
● Reuse: changes in design principles, transportation possibilities, 
standard parts linked to serial numbers and/or types, and/or 
customisation, disassembly plan. 
● Measuring sustainability and circularity. See the guide for 
Measuring Circularity. 
Contractor 
● Extending the service life of assets (possibly with another 
function): technical condition of construction elements, 
construction elements’ loads, residual service life, design 
principles, building physics aspects. 
● Reuse: design principles including changes, transportation 
possibilities, materials, standard parts linked to serial numbers 
and/or types, and/or customisation, disassembly plan.  
● Release of raw materials/materials/parts: when are which raw 
materials released, what is their technical state and residual 
service life, what loads have they been subjected to?
